page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-8GB is an entry-level virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor within UpCloud Cloud Native series. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 1 shared virtual CPU (1 physical core and 1 thread per core), accompanied by 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no bundled local disk storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Synthetic benchmark results reveal polarized computing metrics tied directly to its single shared vCPU allocation. While Geekbench single-core performance registers a competitive 2228.0 points, stress-ng multi-core and single-core compute performance settle at 742.09 points in lower benchmark brackets. System memory bandwidth tests show 16.01 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 13.83 GB/sec for uncached writes. Compression and decompression tests, such as single-threaded gzip (24.25 GB/sec) and bzip3 (9.06 GB/sec), demonstrate middle-tier throughput, whereas Redis set operations record 1.33 million operations per second.

Given the shared single-core limitation and lack of local storage, the instance exhibits a distinct tradeoff between high memory headroom and limited parallel compute capacity. It provides cost-effective resource utilization for applications that require addressable memory without sustained processing load, such as lightweight in-memory caches, development testbeds, background automation jobs, and small non-critical microservices.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-8GB is a KVM-based virtual server designed for lightweight, memory-leaning workloads. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 architecture, the configuration pairs 1 shared vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz with 8.0 GB of RAM, creating a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. Hardware accelerators are absent, and no local storage is bundled with the instance. While single-thread efficiency demonstrates strength in Geekbench benchmarks, multi-core capacity and stress-ng throughput reflect the limitations of a single shared core. Data throughput rates remain modest, with uncached memory reads measuring 16.01 GB/sec and web serving throughput at 1.28 GB/sec. This configuration offers practical cost efficiency for entry-level use cases where memory capacity is prioritized over continuous compute throughput, serving well for lightweight caching layers, development environments, and low-traffic backend utilities.
